articles.title: Two separate mini-Bigfoot sightings reported in an area of Pennsylvania with a history of activity
articles.summary: Two mini-Bigfoot creatures standing just three and a half feet tall were reportedly spotted on a farm in Southwest Pennsylvania, Stan Gordon reports.
articles.body: Reports out of Southwest Pennsylvania indicate that people are seeing some odd creatures wandering around outside. They've been described as Bigfoot encounters, but these aren't your typical 8-foot giants. These are sightings of what Penn Live reports are "mini-Bigfoots." The two separate incidents took place last Tuesday, Aug. 18, and Wednesday, Aug. 19, and involve Bigfoot-like creatures that are no taller than five feet. The first encounter, which was reported to researcher Stan Gordon, took place on a farm in Indiana County, Pennsylvania. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS The witness, Gordon reported, was wrapping up a chore at one of the farm buildings on the property when she heard what sounded like something being thrown around. As she exited the building she "noticed a figure crouching behind trees approximately 60 feet away. She then saw a second, similar figure crouched near the first." She claims the two figures jumped up and started running around as if they were playing. She watched them for several minutes, describing them as walking upright on two legs and standing about three and a half feet tall. "Their bodies were covered with straggly, medium-length, light brown hair," Gordon noted from the witness' account. DAD AND HIS KIDS THINK THEY'VE CAPTURED BIGFOOT ON VIDEO AFTER SPOTTING SOMETHING IN THE WOODS "Neither appeared to have a visible neck. Their heads seemed to rest directly on their shoulders. Their faces were darker brown than the rest of their bodies, and their eyes appeared round and dark brown." The witness, unfortunately, didn’t have her phone with her. But she went on to describe them as having slender arms reminding her of a young child's arms and making noises that sounded like a baby cooing. The encounter came to an end when she sneezed and the two mini-Bigfoot spotted her. She ran home and told her husband about it. The family dog was afraid to go outside after the incident, and she was awakened one night by a sound similar to the cooing she says she heard. Her husband heard loud knocks the day of the sighting, but didn’t witness anything himself. The second of the encounters took place the following night around 8:00 p.m. in Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania. A driver along a rural road says she spotted a creature covered in hair running up a hill. TWO LADIES, A DOG, A LIGHTHOUSE AND A POSSIBLE BIGFOOT ENCOUNTER ON A BEACH IN MICHIGAN The witness only saw the creature for a few seconds, but says she got a good look at it. She estimated the height to be just five feet tall. She says it moved on two legs and was covered with charcoal-gray hair. "Its head was somewhat dome-shaped, with no apparent neck. The arms were long and swung as it moved. Its nose appeared slightly flat with flared nostrils," Gordon noted. "The witness did not notice any ears. Its eyes were small and dark. She saw only one hair-covered leg clearly as the creature spun around and retreated down the hillside." This general area of Pennsylvania has had Bigfoot and UFO sightings before, according to Gordon. But there's nothing to connect these recent sightings with any of those prior reports. OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD The mystery of these purported mini-Bigfoot will likely remain a mystery. As is the case with a lot of sightings, this one did not come with any supporting physical evidence. Not even a blurry picture of what is probably a shadow. If there are any further mini-Bigfoot sightings or any sightings of Bigfoot at all, for that matter, OutKick OutDoors will be on top of it. If you have your own sighting to share or come across anything, send it my way sean.joseph@outkick.com.

articles.title: Let's look back on the best moments (read: crashes) from the World Humanoid Robot Games
articles.summary: Videos from the World Humanoid Robot Games show android athletes crashing, boxing, and high-jumping in hilarious fashion as algorithms spread the clips.
articles.body: Social media algorithms can be a treacherous thing, but sometimes they just bring pure, unleaded delight, as has been the case with videos from the World Humanoid Robot Games. My usual Instagram feed full of guitars, motorsports news, and clips from Amish softball games (which are phenomenal, by the way) was suddenly hijacked by video after video of humanoid robots hitting the track, boxing, and high-jumping at their human masters' bidding. It's a beautiful thing... until they snap and enslave us all, but damn, until then it's hilarious. CHINESE ROBOT BREAKS HUMAN WORLD RECORD IN BEIJING HALF-MARATHON So, with the Games drawing to a close, I wanted to take a walk down memory lane at some of the Games' best moments. Sure, there was the bot that beat Usain Bolt's 100-meter record, but I prefer the more light-hearted lowlights. I'm talking about any video in which the 100-meter-running bots crash into a pad because, despite the incredible tech on display, no one has figured out how to give these android athletes any kind of braking procedure. HUMANOID ROBOTS JUST GOT A WORKPLACE SAFETY SYSTEM Now, I don't mean to sit here and play armchair robotics expert, but how is it that not one poindexter in the robot-building bunch has worked out a sensor that tells the robot it's about to plow into a crash pad? Think of cars with adaptive cruise control or even fully driverless cars. Yet, with that tech available, the best we can do for those robots is treat them like crash test dummies? HUMANOID ROBOT SKIN SENSES PEOPLE BEFORE CONTACT I'd want to enslave humanity too, if that was how I was treated. But, hey, I still love the crashes. When they happen, the sensors that are on board go completely haywire and send the bots into some kind of Raygun Olympic breakdancing routine. No one had a worse time, however, than this poor bot who competed in weightlifting and gave us the biggest choke job of all time. Poor guy... probably got swirlied in the locker room too. What an event and what a content factory the World Humanoid Robot Games proved to be. articles.title: Italian Festival returns to Endicott for 19th year running
articles.summary: ENDICOTT, N.Y. (WIVT/WBGH) – Get ready to savor the sounds and flavors of Little Italy this Friday. GUSTO! Italian Festival is returning to the Northside of...
articles.body:
ENDICOTT, N.Y. (WIVT/WBGH) - Get ready to savor the sounds and flavors of Little Italy this Friday.

GUSTO! Italian Festival is returning to the Northside of Endicott for its 19th year.

The festival continues to grow in terms of its attendance, footprint and number of vendors, over 40 this year.

The primary focus is on Italian food, with meatballs, pizza, sausage and peppers, lamb spiedies and a wide variety of Italian desserts and pastries. Although there will be Greek and soul food vendors as well.

There will also be a wide variety of live music on multiple stages.

Little Italy Endicott Board Member Loreta Paniccia says GUSTO! helps bring awareness to the group's efforts to revitalize the neighborhood.

"GUSTO! is a capstone activity that we hold. A community event that brings in support to our vendors and our businesses, but it's more attention to our bigger mission which is supporting our neighborhood and continuing to build community and enhancing this area as much as we can," Paniccia says.

There will also be plenty of fun activities for kids including face painting, arts and crafts, yard games and magic shows.

The evening will conclude with a fireworks show over George W. Johnson Park.

GUSTO! runs from 4:30 p.m. to 9 p.m. Friday and is free to attend.

articles.title: Rockstar finally releases statement regarding ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ leaks, leaving fans even more confused
articles.summary: Rockstar Games broke its silence on the "Grand Theft Auto VI" leaks, but key phrases in the statement sparked an uproar among frustrated fans.
articles.body: Last week, a series of gameplay leaks of the much anticipated "Grand Theft Auto VI" captivated the video game community. A social media account by the name of CyberLeek posted a number of videos playing what appeared to be a full build of the game, including one in which they flew an airplane through downtown Vice City, a fictionalized version of Miami. Game developer Rockstar remained silent for nearly a week after the leaks, despite CyberLeek’s continued calls for them to respond. GAMING-WORLD VETERAN WHO RIPPED ‘WOKE’ CULTURE SCORES TRUMP-BACKED BATTLEGROUND PRIMARY WIN Wednesday morning, however, Rockstar Games broke its silence, releasing a statement and giving an update on the game’s status in the wake of the leaks. In case you couldn’t figure it out just by skimming through it, the statement didn’t go over well with many of the gaming community, as several key phrases caught fans’ attention in a negative way. For starters, Rockstar calling the leaks "heartbreaking" had plenty of fans all over the internet rolling their eyes. The big one that had everyone in an uproar, though, was toward the end of the first paragraph, where Rockstar revealed the game still isn’t finished. A game that has taken 13 years to complete still isn’t quite ready yet, and that caused fans to explode. Another line that caused some confusion was at the end of the second paragraph, where Rockstar says, "we hope everyone will wait a little bit longer to experience the game for themselves on November 19." Some fans incorrectly assumed that meant another delay was in the works, but I don’t believe that to be the case. With Rockstar's track record, I could see how that would be the thought process from fans. THE FIVE BEST YEARS IN VIDEO GAME HISTORY RANKED: WHICH GAMING YEAR WAS THE GREATEST EVER? Others thought the leaks and subsequent negative public response caused the developers to panic and go back to fixing the game, but this far into things I doubt that's what this is all about. Regardless of what Rockstar thought it would achieve by releasing this statement, it did little to quell the bloodlust from fans who have felt scorned by the once-beloved developer. Gamers have felt burned by the seemingly exorbitant wait for the next big Grand Theft Auto game as well as the announcement earlier this year that the game would be released solely as a digital game with no physical disc to accompany it. This was the genesis for CyberLeek’s avalanche of gameplay leaks over the past week, claiming to do so on behalf of gamers everywhere who felt as though Rockstar disregarded their core demographic with these choices and delays. One thing is for sure, we haven’t seen the last of this saga. articles.title: Why Dolly Parton could bring together Americans who agree on almost nothing
articles.summary: Dolly Parton embodied the African concept of Ubuntu — "I am because we are" — enlarging humanity through her Imagination Library and delight in others.
articles.body: Throughout her life, Dolly Parton kept reminding me of something beautiful about being human. Perhaps you noticed it too. Her death has brought an outpouring of affection from people who otherwise might agree on very little. And it leaves me wondering: What was it about Dolly? Talent alone doesn't explain it. Success doesn't explain it. Even her extraordinary generosity doesn't fully explain it. DOLLY PARTON DIES AT THE AGE OF 80: A LOOK AT HER LIFE THROUGH PHOTOS I suspect we recognized something deeper — a way of being human that somehow enlarged the humanity around her. Many years ago, my friend Archbishop Desmond Tutu introduced me to an African word that has stayed with me ever since: Ubuntu. It is often translated as "I am because we are." Over time, I have experienced Ubuntu less as a definition and more as a way of moving through the world. It is the quiet conviction that another person's life can become larger because you showed up. It is the belief that another person's humanity matters too much to be reduced to a label, a failure, a fear or someone else's judgment. Dolly Parton struck me as someone who intuitively Ubuntued her way through life. DOLLY PARTON'S ‘ALL-AMERICAN HEART’: HOW COUNTRY ICON FORGED SPECIAL BOND WITH US MILITARY In an America increasingly divided into competing camps and tribes, she was one of our great exceptions. Conservatives admired her. Liberals admired her. Christians admired her. People with no religious affiliation admired her. Rural America admired her. Urban America admired her. Dolly Parton is gone. But what we loved in her isn't. She seemed to delight in people. She didn't require that people become more like her before she could enjoy them. Want to have some of what Dolly had? Lean into Ubuntu. Most of us know what it feels like to be reduced to a label, a mistake, a fear or someone else's judgment. And most of us have encountered someone who refused to leave us there. Perhaps you've known someone who saw more in you than the labels that had been placed upon you. Perhaps you've encountered someone who made it feel safe to speak in your own voice. DOLLY PARTON'S LIFE IN HER OWN WORDS: FROM SMOKY MOUNTAINS POVERTY TO COUNTRY MUSIC IMMORTALITY Perhaps you've known what it feels like when another person's belief in you arrived before your belief in yourself. Perhaps you've known someone who called forth a larger version of yourself than you could yet imagine. People like this leave us feeling more alive. Perhaps that's because we are not completed in isolation. We are enlarged through encounter. I have yet to meet anyone who isn't carrying more than they should. Maybe that's why another person's humanity can feel so nourishing. Someone sees us. Believes in us. Delights in us. And something in us comes alive. I have no idea whether Dolly Parton ever heard the word Ubuntu. But I suspect she understood it instinctively. Her Imagination Library put hundreds of millions of books into the hands of children, most of whom she would never meet. The number is extraordinary. But perhaps more revealing is what it says about her: She believed in the possibilities of children she did not know. We saw that same instinct in the way she encountered people — in her easy laughter, her delight in others and her apparent belief that the person in front of her mattered. She used her success to enlarge possibilities for people far beyond herself. Dolly Ubuntued. One of the things I love most about Ubuntu is that nobody has to qualify for it. There is no means test, no dress code, no success code, no educational requirement, no preferred political party, no preferred religion, no preferred heritage, no preferred ZIP code, no VIP entrance and no secret handshake. Bring your humanity. That's it. We are changed, nourished, challenged and enlarged through our encounters with one another — sometimes most unexpectedly by people whose lives seem different from our own. In a world that constantly encourages us to sort, rank, label and separate ourselves from one another, Ubuntu offers an astonishing possibility: None of us becomes fully human alone. Your humanity strengthens mine while mine expands yours. We need one another's humanity in order to thrive. Ubuntu may help us survive difficult seasons. But its deeper promise is that we flourish. Not despite one another. Through one another. The older I get, the more convinced I become that this is not simply a beautiful idea. It is a practical truth. We are changed, nourished, challenged and enlarged through our encounters with one another — sometimes most unexpectedly by people whose lives seem different from our own. And we don't encounter this only in people whose names the world knows. It appears in teachers and neighbors, nurses and firefighters, grandparents and lifelong friends and complete strangers. In someone who saw more in you than you could see in yourself. In someone whose humanity surprised you because their life seemed so different from your own. And chances are, you've been that person for someone else. Ubuntu is not merely a word. It's a human thing — a way of helping one another flourish, of becoming more fully ourselves and of discovering that neither of us necessarily leaves an encounter unchanged. Humanity is one of the few things in life that grows when it is shared. When we strengthen another person's humanity, we strengthen our own. Dolly Parton is gone. But what we loved in her isn't. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION It is still possible every time someone refuses to reduce another person to a label. Every time someone believes in another person before that person can believe in themselves. Every time one human being calls forth something larger in another — and discovers that they, too, have been enlarged. Maybe that's some of what Dolly was showing us all along. So let's celebrate humanity. Let's celebrate the people who enlarge it. You've been Ubuntued. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Perhaps you've Ubuntued others. Let's Ubuntu together.

articles.title: Busy Philipps diagnosed with rare brain tumor after undergoing body scan her doctor told her she didn't 'need'
articles.summary: Busy Phillips revealed her grade 2 oligodendroglioma diagnosis came after a Prenuvo scan her primary care doctor initially said she didn't need.
articles.body: Busy Philipps is sharing how she was diagnosed with a rare brain tumor. During a recent interview with People magazine, the 47-year-old "Cougar Town" actress shared the terrifying moment her doctor told her she had a brain tumor, the day after her "Dawson's Creek" co-star, James Van Der Beek, died after a battle with colorectal cancer. "Dr. Devinsky says to me, 'I'm just going to say this to you the way I would want someone to say it to me,'" she recalled. 'BACHELORETTE' STAR REVEALS BRAIN TUMOR DIAGNOSIS AFTER ROUTINE HEALTH SCAN "And that was when the wind like sort of knocked out of me, and I had to sit down. He was like, 'I need you to breathe. I can hear that you're not breathing.' And I was like, 'Just tell me what's happening.' And he's like, 'This isn't any of those other things that they said it could be. This is a real tumor, and it's inside your brain, and Busy, it's got to come out. We got to take it out.'" She was then connected with Dr. John Golfinos of NYU Langone and scheduled the five-hour surgery for March 2, during which surgeons removed a 2.6-centimeter mass from her brain. The mass was then biopsied and revealed to be a grade 2 oligodendroglioma, a rare tumor that Dr. Alexandra Miller, Philipps’s neuro-oncologist at NYU Langone told People, affects 1,100 to 1,300 people a year in the U.S. She added that "it is considered malignant, but it has the best prognosis of all of the malignant gliomas." "It’s sort of defined as a cancerous tumor based on the ability of the tumor to regrow over time, rather than it looking very malignant under the microscope," Miller said. The diagnosis came after Philipps told her cousin’s husband, a doctor in Los Angeles, that she was interested in getting a Prenuvo scan but that her primary care doctor had told her in 2025, "You're super healthy. We've done all this other blood work. We've done, like, all kinds of tests. You're super healthy. There's no need for you to get one." "'Oh, I love them,'" he told Philipps about the scan. "And I was like, 'OK, cause my doctor just a few months ago said that I shouldn't get one.' He's like, 'Oh, like respectfully, don't know your doctor, but disagree. I think knowledge is power.' "And what he said really resonated with me. And I was like, 'That was kind of what I was feeling, too. I think I want to get one.' He's like, 'Well, I'd be happy to help you set that up.'" GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE After getting the scan, the "Freaks and Geeks" star went to an audition and later that night got a call from her cousin's husband, who let her know there was a lesion on her brain and that she should get an MRI. Dr. Devinsky later told her the MRI showed a tumor that needed to be removed. Philipps’ neurosurgeon, Dr. John Golfinos, told People that the early detection of the tumor ultimately made the surgery much easier, adding that had the tumor been found later, it "would have been two or three times the size." Over a month after recovery, Philipps was back on the operating table after her dermatologist flagged that her incision site looked concerning. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE She had contracted staphylococcus, which required another surgery to cure, leaving Philipps feeling "really upset" and "like I was back at square one." Despite her health scares, Philipps still managed to film her upcoming legal drama, "Cupertino," in which she plays the ex-wife of an AI billionaire who becomes the financier of a new law firm. Philipps does not need chemotherapy or radiation but will get regular scans to monitor any potential reoccurrence. Through this experience, the actress learned to trust her instincts. articles.body:
Um longa-metragem produzido por cineastas do Distrito Federal pode representar o Brasil na disputa pelo Oscar 2027 .

"A natureza das coisas invisíveis" , dirigido por Rafaela Camelo, aparece entre os 15 filmes selecionados pela Academia Brasileira de Cinema para concorrer a uma vaga como representante do país na categoria de Melhor Filme Internacional.

➡ Em 9 de setembro, a Comissão de Seleção vai se reunir para selecionar seis dos 15 longas para uma pré-lista.

O filme é uma coprodução com o Chile e teve financiamento do Fundo de Apoio à Cultura do Distrito Federal (FAC). Já a primeira exibição do DF foi em 2025, como encerramento do 58º Festival de Brasília do Cinema Brasileiro .

Antes, a obra havia ganhado três categorias no Festival de Cinema de Gramado.

A Natureza das Coisas Invisíveis (2025) — Foto: Divulgação

Daniela Marinho, produtora do longa, comemorou a recepção pelo público da capital e destacou a importância de incentivos culturais. “Foi uma sessão [no Cine Brasília] em que metade do público não conseguiu entrar, foi uma loucura”, conta.

“Cabe a nós celebrar e fazer a corrente para que o filme seja selecionado. Não é sempre que a gente tem a oportunidade de ver nossa história, nossos rostos e nossas tradições nas telas”, afirma.

Brasília também aparece em outro selecionado pela Academia, dessa vez como cenário. "A conspiração Condor", de André Sturm, mostra imagens da capital nos anos 1960, durante a ditadura militar.

A trajetória de " A natureza das coisas invisíveis" começou ainda em 2019, com a elaboração do projeto, mas as gravações iniciaram em 2023.

Para Daniela, o momento é de recompensa pelo esforço empenhado na obra. "A gente se planejou e se programou muito para estar nesse lugar", comenta.

A produtora destaca que o filme só foi pssível por meio das políticas de incentivo à cultura, como o FAC, e lamenta o desmonte nos investimentos em cinema no DF.

Cineastas apontam atraso no repasse aos filmes contemplados no FAC Audiovisual. O resultado do edital saiu em dezembro, mas nenhum pagamento foi emitido desde então.

Em julho, a falta de repasses afetou o Cine Brasília, único cinema de rua do Distrito Federal. A 59ª edição do Festival de Brasília do Cinema Brasileiro também esteve ameaçada pela falta de recursos.

O cancelamento seria o primeiro desde 1974, quando o evento foi cancelado em protesto à ditadura militar.

Além do longa brasiliense, veja os filmes que podem se tornar o "candidato do Brasil" para Melhor Filme Internacional no Oscar 2027:

"A fabulosa máquina do tempo", de Eliza Capai

"A natureza das coisas invisíveis", de Rafaela Camelo

"Ato noturno", de Marcio Reolon e Filipe Matzembacher

"Dolores", de Maria Clara Escobar e Marcelo Gomes

"Herança de Narcisa", de Clarissa Appelt e Daniel Dias

"Quando vira a esquina", de Chris Alcazar

"Vicentina pede desculpas", de Gabriel Martin

articles.body: Yash starrer 'Toxic' released in cinemas after much anticipation on Wednesday and it did meet expections! History has been rewritten by Yash, as 'Toxic' has set the box office on fire with a phenomenal opening day. Making his much-awaited return to the big screen after the blockbuster success of 'KGF: Chapter 2', the pan-India star has delivered a massive start with the Geetu Mohandas directorial crossing the Rs 100 crore mark in India on day one itself.Toxic Movie ReviewAccording to Sacnilk, 'Toxic' has earned an estimated Rs 101.10 crore net in India on its opening day across all languages. The film was released in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam, while its India gross collection has reportedly touched Rs 140 crore. This is the second best opening for an Indian film after 'Dhurandhar 2' which made Rs 103 crore on day 1.With this spectacular opening, Yash has once again proved his immense box office pull. After kickstarting the Rs 100 crore opening-day trend with 'K.G.F: Chapter 2', the actor has now delivered another film in the same league. If 'Ramayana' also manages to achieve the feat this year, Yash could become the first star to score three Rs 100 crore openers in such quick succession, further cementing his status as one of Indian cinema's biggest box office forces.'Toxic' box office collection Day 2 [LIVE]: Can Yash and Kiara Advani film cross Rs 150 crore after smashing Ranveer Singh led 'Dhurandhar's opening record?Meanwhile, 'Awarapan 2' which was doing well in theatres so far, saw a magnificent drop with the release of 'Toxic'. While the number of shows of the Emraan Hashmi film were also reduced, it ended up making Rs 90 lakhs on day 13. On Tuesday, day 12, it had made Rs 3.75 crore.Clearly, the film will now near the end of its run soon with the release of the Yash starrer. 'Batwara 1947' now ends it theatrical run with Rs 37.77 crore in India.Now it all depends on word of mouth whether 'Toxic' will be able to grow in the coming days. There have been mixed reviews for the film but the momentum which is now built should remain till the weekend.Helmed by Geetu Mohandas, 'Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups' features an impressive ensemble led by Rocking Star Yash, with Nayanthara, Kiara Advani, Tara Sutaria, Rukmini Vasanth and Huma Qureshi in prominent roles. articles.title: O que fazer no Rio: shows de graça, samba e teatro até 2 de setembro | G1
articles.standfirst: Programação entre os dias 27 de agosto a 2 de setembro reúne shows, teatro, exposições e atividades para crianças.
articles.summary: A agenda com o que fazer no Rio destaca shows gratuitos de Toquinho e Roberta Sá, samba na Lapa e o festival Arte Core no MAM de 27 de agosto a 2 de setembro.
articles.body:
A programação cultural do Rio nos próximos dias tem dois festivais multiculturais com shows e outras atrações no Museu do Pontal (29 e 30) e no Parque das Figueiras, na Lagoa (28 a 30).

Entre as apresentações musicais do evento do aniversário do Museu do Pontal estão Siba e Edimilson dos Teclados no sábado (29) e do Trio Forrozão no domingo (30). Já o Festival Harmonia, na Lagoa, terá entre seus shows Toquinho na sexta-feira (28), a Orquestra Petrobras Sinfônica sábado (29) e Roberta Sá domingo (30).

Outros destaques no Rio estão uma de samba com Wander Pires sexta-feira (28) no Casarão do Firmino e o festival Arte Core, que une artes plásticas a esporte e música no MAM.

Veja abaixo os eventos e monte seu roteiro:

O cantor e compositor Danilo Cutrim, conhecido por estar à frente das bandas Forfun e Braza, apresenta seu show solo no Dolores Club na sexta-feira (28). A apresentação marca uma nova fase na carreira do artista e constrói uma narrativa de transformação, promovendo um encontro sonoro entre a atmosfera íntima e contemplativa do trabalho "Azul" e a energia de "Neon", seu próximo projeto.

🗓️ Quando? Sexta-feira (28 de agosto), às 20h30 (abertura da casa às 19h)📍 Onde? Dolores Club - Rua do Lavradio, 10, Centro💲 Quanto? A partir de R$ 60.

O Museu do Pontal celebra seus 50 anos de dedicação à arte popular brasileira com um festival no sábado e domingo (29 e 30). A programação gratuita marca a abertura da exposição "Véio – A Escuta do Sertão", a maior retrospectiva já feita sobre o renomado escultor sergipano, e a realização de um festival que exalta a diversidade cultural do país. O evento conta com mais de 20 atrações, incluindo shows de ícones como a mestra Lia de Itamaracá, Siba, Mestre Solano e Trio Forrozão, além de manifestações tradicionais como bumba meu boi, folia de reis, capoeira, circo e atividades voltadas para o público infantil.

Programação de Sábado — 29/08 - 10h — Dança Mineiro Pau Valdemar Madalena 10h / 14h30 — Brincadeiras 11h30 — Encontro de Capoeira 14h30 — Cinema: José Bezerra, Artista 15h — Show Zé Bezerra + Trio Pernambucano 15h30 — Abertura: Véio: a escuta do sertão 16h30 — Folias de Reis 17h30 — Performance Bate-bola Brilhetes de Anchieta 18h — Show Siba 19h30 — Edmilson dos Teclados 20h15 — Show Lia de Itamaracá + Quarteto da Ciranda 11h / 13h / 15h / 16h — Visitas musicadas 10h–20h15 — DJ Xeleléu

Domingo — 30/08 - 11h — O Mirabolante Homem Bola 12h — Espetáculo Solo Protocolo 13h15 — Cinema: Artistas Cazumbas 13h45 — Boi Muleque Garboso 14h45 — Oficina com Rona 15h30 — Show Mestre Solano + Noites do Norte 16h — Oficina Dobraduras 17h — Show Aturiá 18h30 — Show Trio Forrozão 10h / 11h / 12h — Bebês no Museu 11h / 13h / 15h / 16h30 — Visitas musicadas 14h45–20h30 — DJ Nego Sensível

🗓️ Quando? Sábado (29) e domingo (30 de agosto), a partir das 10h📍 Onde? Museu do Pontal (Avenida Celia Ribeiro da Silva Mendes, 3.300, Barra da Tijuca)💲 Quanto? Entrada gratuita🧒 Classificação: Livre (com atividades específicas até para bebês).

A festa Rebobina toma conta do Palco Dolores, no Rio Scenarium, no sábado (29) para uma noite totalmente dedicada ao flashback. O evento propõe uma verdadeira viagem musical pelas décadas de 70, 80 e 90, resgatando sucessos da disco music, pop, rock, grunge, eurodance e hip-hop. O comando das picapes fica por conta do VDJ Roberto Sabino, DJ Zé Mele e DJ Gustavo Jr..

🗓️ Quando? Sábado (29 de agosto), a partir das 20h📍 Onde? Palco Dolores – Rio Scenarium (Rua do Lavradio, 20, Centro💲 Quanto? A partir de R$ 30 (antecipado).

Festival Harmonia no Parque das Figueiras

Festival Harmonia no Parque das Figueiras — Foto: Divulgação

O Festival Harmonia chega à sua 4ª edição no Parque das Figueiras, na Lagoa Rodrigo de Freitas, entre sexta-feira (28) e domingo (30). Com o conceito de celebrar a pluralidade cultural e a riqueza dos seis biomas brasileiros (Amazônia, Caatinga, Cerrado, Mata Atlântica, Pampa e Pantanal), o evento gratuito une música, alta gastronomia, sustentabilidade, arte e economia criativa em uma festa ao ar livre. O público poderá desfrutar de feirinhas de produtores locais, oficinas criativas, aulas de culinária e ilhas gastronômicas comandadas por chefs renomados, como Erick Jacquin, Bel Coelho e Heaven Delhaye. A programação musical terá na sexta-feira (28) Rafael Sperduto e Toquinho com Camila Faustino; o sábado (29) conta com a Orquestra Petrobras Sinfônica, Leoni e DJ Jamal; e o domingo (30) encerra com Roberta Sá, Serjão Loroza e DJ Jamal.

🗓️ Quando? De sexta a domingo (28 a 30 de agosto)📍 Onde? Parque das Figueiras (Lagoa Rodrigo de Freitas)💲 Quanto? Entrada gratuita.🧒 Classificação: Livre.

A Areninha Cultural Hermeto Pascoal, em Bangu, recebe neste sábado, (29), uma noite que une música pesada e mobilização social com shows das bandas Ratos de Porão, Sangria e Cervical. Além das apresentações, o evento promove uma campanha de arrecadação de alimentos e uma parceria com o projeto CAIS ComCausa para marcar o Dia Internacional de Conscientização sobre a Sobredosagem. O espaço contará com uma barraca e ações informativas sobre redução de danos, prevenção, acesso a direitos e combate ao estigma relacionado ao uso de álcool e outras drogas.

🗓️ Quando? Sábado (29), a partir das 18h📍 Onde? Areninha Cultural Hermeto Pascoal - Praça Primeiro de Maio, s/n, Bangu, Rio de Janeiro 💲 Quanto? R$ 40.

O consagrado intérprete Wander Pires comanda mais uma edição de sua roda de samba no Casarão do Firmino, na Lapa, nesta sexta-feira (28). O cantor apresenta um repertório que mistura clássicos do pagode romântico e sambas-enredo que marcaram época. A noite conta ainda com show de abertura do grupo Peso do Samba, participação especial de Wandinho Pires (filho de Wander) e intervalos comandados pela DJ Nicolle Neumann.

🗓️ Quando? Sexta-feira (28), a partir das 18h (chopp liberado das 18h às 19h30)📍 Onde? Casarão do Firmino - Rua da Relação, 19, Lapa💲 Quanto? Entrada colaborativa (contribuição financeira voluntária, o público paga o quanto puder ou achar justo)🧒 Classificação: 10 anos (menores devem apresentar documento oficial e estar acompanhados pelos responsáveis legais).

Reinauguração do Espaço Arlindo Cruz com Pagode do Luna

O Espaço Arlindo Cruz, em Realengo, reabre suas portas nesta sexta-feira (28) com a estreia da roda de samba Pagode do Luna. A noite terá também convidados surpresa, além do DJ Sorriso comandando os intervalos.

🗓️ Quando? Sexta-feira (28), a partir das 20h📍 Onde? Espaço Arlindo Cruz - Rua Marechal Joaquim Inácio, s/nº, embaixo do viaduto de Realengo, Zona Oeste do Rio💲 Quanto? Entrada gratuita até as 21h. Após esse horário, os ingressos custam R$ 15 (vendas pelo Sympla). O copo personalizado do evento custa R$ 5.

O grupo de pagode Menos é Mais desembarca no Rio de Janeiro com a turnê “Churrasquinho -+” no sábado (29). Com um show de quatro horas de duração, o evento reúne os maiores sucessos da carreira do grupo, como “P do Pecado”, “Coração Partido” e “Brinda Aê”, além de contar com convidados especiais.

🗓️ Quando? Sábado (29), abertura dos portões às 14h📍 Onde? Gramado do Riocentro - Av. Salvador Allende, 6555, Barra Olímpica💲 Quanto? O evento conta com dois setores. No "Arena", os valores vão de 230 a 460 reais. Já o "Full Open Bar Premium Skol" o valor é de 550 reais – ambos no lote atual.

“Festa no Arraial, O Musical” chega ao Rio após temporada em São Paulo e ocupa o Teatro Clara Nunes, na Gávea, de 21 de agosto a 27 de setembro. Livremente inspirado em “Sonho de uma Noite de Verão”, de William Shakespeare, o espetáculo transporta a história para uma vila nordestina em meio às festas juninas. A trama mistura romance, comédia e fantasia, com 14 atores, cantores e instrumentistas no elenco. Claudia Ohana, Lorena Tucci, Cadu Libonati e Bernardo Mesquita estão entre os nomes do elenco. As sessões acontecem às sextas, sábados e domingos.

🗓️ Quando? De 21 de agosto a 27 de setembro. Sextas, às 20h; sábados, às 17h30; e domingos, às 16h📍 Onde? Teatro Clara Nunes — Shopping da Gávea, Rua Marquês de São Vicente, 52, loja 370, Gávea💲 Quanto? De R$ 25 a R$ 140 🔞 Classificação: Livre.

O espetáculo inédito “Gosto Amargo na Pele”, d’Os Ciclomáticos Companhia de Teatro, estreia no Rio nesta quinta-feira (20). Com dramaturgia e direção de Ribamar Ribeiro, a montagem é uma adaptação da vida e da obra de Plínio Marcos e encerra a Trilogia dos Indesejáveis, do grupo. A peça passa pelo Teatro Glauce Rocha e, em setembro, segue para o Teatro Firjan SESI Centro, onde terá 14 apresentações. Em cena, o espetáculo aborda temas como desigualdade, exclusão, violência e resistência a partir de personagens ligados ao universo retratado pelo dramaturgo.

🗓️ Quando? De 20 a 28 de agosto, no Teatro Glauce Rocha; de 24 de setembro a 4 de outubro, no Teatro Firjan SESI Centro. 📍 Onde? Teatro Glauce Rocha — Av. Rio Branco, 179, Centro; Teatro Firjan SESI Centro — Av. Graça Aranha, 1, Centro. 💲 Quanto? R$ 20 (inteira) e R$ 10 (meia) no Glauce Rocha; R$ 40 (inteira) e R$ 20 (meia) no Firjan SESI. 🔞 Classificação: 18 anos.

O musical "Wicked – A História Não Contada das Bruxas de Oz" é estrelada por Myra Ruiz (Elphaba) e Fabi Bang (Glinda) e revela a história de amizade e os caminhos que moldaram o destino das bruxas muito antes da chegada de Dorothy ao mundo governado pelo Mágico de Oz. O espetáculo une a narrativa a uma montagem marcada por inovação tecnológica, efeitos de ilusionismo, projeções e sistemas de 'voo'.

🗓️ Quando? Até 6 de setembro. Sessões: Quartas, quintas e sextas, às 20h; sábados, às 15h e 19h30; domingos, às 14h e 18h30📍 Onde? Cidade das Artes Bibi Ferreira - Av. das Américas, 5300 - Barra da Tijuca💲 Quanto? De R$ 50 a R$ 400. Ingressos à venda no site Sympla e na bilheteria do local🧒 Classificação: Livre (menores de 12 anos devem estar acompanhados dos pais ou responsáveis legais).

O youtuber Gato Galactico apresenta seu novo espetáculo ao vivo, "O Reino Mágico", no domingo (30). Com música, dança e uma experiência imersiva, o show celebra o poder dos sonhos e a imaginação infantil. No palco, o público vai reencontrar personagens como Roni, Luna, Mimi e o Gato Lunático, navegando por universos lúdicos já conhecidos pelas crianças, como Patrulha Estelar e Prismágicos.

🗓️ Quando? Domingo (30 de agosto), às 17h📍 Onde? Qualistage - Via Parque Shopping - Av. Ayrton Senna, 3000, Barra da Tijuca💲 Quanto? A partir de R$ 50🧒 Classificação: Livre.

O Tablado abre a programação de 75 anos com nova montagem do texto de Maria Clara Machado. A peça acompanha Ângela, uma bruxinha que estuda em uma escola de maldades, mas não consegue agir como as outras e acaba ajudando um menino da floresta. Com direção e adaptação de Cacá Mourthé, o espetáculo retoma um dos títulos mais conhecidos do teatro infantil brasileiro em temporada na Lagoa.

🗓️Quando? Até 13 de setembro, sábados e domingos, às 17h. 📍Onde? Teatro O Tablado - Av. Lineu de Paula Machado, 795, Lagoa. 💲Quanto? De R$ 40 a R$ 80. 🧒Classificação: Livre.

Ritinha Rock & Roll - Rita Lee para Crianças

O musical infantil apresenta uma história inspirada na trajetória e na obra de Rita Lee. Em cena, uma menina que sonha em mudar o mundo pela música enfrenta situações na escola e em defesa dos animais, em uma trama sobre imaginação, liberdade e expressão. O espetáculo integra o projeto “Grandes Músicos para Pequenos” e tem texto de Pedro Henrique Lopes, direção de Diego Morais e direção musical de Guilherme Borges.

🗓️Quando? Até 6 de setembro, sábados e domingos, às 16h. 📍Onde? EcoVilla Ri Happy - Rua Jardim Botânico, 1008, Jardim Botânico. 💲Quanto? Plateia VIP: R$ 60 (meia-entrada); Plateia Lateral: R$ 50 (meia-entrada). 🧒Classificação: Livre.

O musical infantil acompanha duas crianças que são levadas para o fundo da Baía de Guanabara e encontram animais aquáticos em meio à poluição das águas. A peça aborda preservação ambiental e vida marinha com canções inéditas. O espetáculo foi criado por Diego Morais e Pedro Henrique Lopes, com músicas de Tony Lucchesi e Marcelo Mendonça. As apresentações acontecem em formato de temporada de fim de semana.

🗓️Quando? Até 6 de setembro, sábados e domingos, às 11h. 📍Onde? EcoVilla Ri Happy - Rua Jardim Botânico, 1008, Jardim Botânico. 💲Quanto? Plateia VIP: R$ 45 (meia-entrada); Plateia Lateral: R$ 35 (meia-entrada). 🧒Classificação: Livre.

Festival Arte Core — Foto: Divulgação/I Hate Flash

Após cinco anos, o festival Arte Core retorna para sua nona edição no sábado e domingo (29 e 30), transformando o Museu de Arte Moderna do Rio de Janeiro (MAM Rio) em um grande polo de cultura urbana e contemporânea. O evento reúne artes visuais, skate, moda e oficinas práticas. A programação inclui a estreia da feira de arte impressa Arte Craft, ativações de marcas (como moda circular com a Pool Jeans e uma galeria de artistas suburbanos promovida pela Kenner), além de muita música com DJs de vinil e shows dos rappers BNegão e FBC.

🗓️ Quando? Dias 29 e 30 de agosto de 2026. (Show do FBC a partir das 21h)📍 Onde? Museu de Arte Moderna do Rio de Janeiro - MAM Rio (Av. Infante Dom Henrique, 85, Parque do Flamengo)💲 Quanto? Grátis (mediante retirada de ingressos disponíveis para retirada pela Sympla a partir das 11h do dia 25)🧒 Classificação: Livre.

A Casa Brasil promove neste sábado (29) uma roda de conversa gratuita com o artista Thomaz Velho, a curadora Adriana Nakamuta e a jornalista Domi Valansi. O encontro propõe um bate-papo com o público sobre a trajetória do artista, a importância cultural do Centro do Rio e os bastidores e desafios de montagem da exposição "Tormenta", que apresenta obras inéditas de grandes proporções e marca uma nova fase na pesquisa visual do artista. A mostra segue em cartaz no local até o dia 6 de setembro.

🗓️ Quando? Sábado (29), às 15h. A exposição "Tormenta" pode ser visitada até 6 de setembro (de terça a domingo, das 10h às 17h)📍 Onde? Casa Brasil - Rua Visconde de Itaboraí, 78, Centro, Rio de Janeiro)💲 Quanto? Entrada gratuita🧒 Classificação: Livre.

O Galpão das Artes Urbanas Helio G. Pellegrino recebe a exposição “Upcycling: Seu Lixo Vira Arte”, do artista e designer carioca David Dahis. A mostra reúne 15 obras, entre esculturas, miniaturas, mosaicos e luminárias, produzidas com materiais que seriam descartados. A proposta é mostrar como objetos do cotidiano podem ganhar novas funções sem perder suas características originais. Entre as peças estão uma boate em miniatura feita a partir de uma caixa de chocolates, um telão construído com um iPad quebrado e um globo de espelhos produzido com uma semente.

🗓️ Quando? A partir de sexta-feira (28), das 9h às 17h📍 Onde? Galpão das Artes Urbanas Helio G. Pellegrino – Av. Padre Leonel Franca, s/nº, Gávea (embaixo do viaduto Lagoa-Barra)💲 Entrada: gratuita

A exposição imersiva reúne projeções em 360 graus , instalações e ambientes inspirados nas obras de Gustav Klimt e Antoni Gaudí. O percurso propõe uma experiência sensorial com imagens em grande escala, música e espaços interativos que dialogam com a pintura de Klimt e a arquitetura de Gaudí.

Entre os destaques, estão simulações do interior da Sagrada Família e da fachada da Casa Batlló, além de réplicas de elementos ligados à obra do arquiteto catalão.

O núcleo dedicado a Klimt traz projeções de trabalhos como “O Beijo”, “Retrato de Adele Bloch-Bauer” e “Morte e Vida”, em um pavilhão montado no Rio Design Barra.

🗓️ Quando? Terça a sábado, das 10h às 22h; domingos e feriados, das 12h às 21h. 📍 Onde? Rio Design Barra - Av. das Américas, 7777 – Barra da Tijuca. 💲 Quanto? Terça a sexta, até 17h30: R$ 90 (inteira) e R$ 45 (meia). Terça a sexta, a partir de 18h: R$ 110 (inteira) e R$ 55 (meia). Sábados, domingos e feriados: R$ 130 (inteira) e R$ 65 (meia). Crianças de até 4 anos não pagam. Antecipados pelo site. 🔞 Classificação: livre.

'Um século de Metrópolis: da invenção do futuro às ruínas do sonho moderno'

Última semana da mostra de cinema que tem como ponto de partida os 100 anos de “Metrópolis”, de Fritz Lang, e reúne 69 filmes de diferentes épocas e países. A seleção aborda temas como modernidade, urbanização, tecnologia, trabalho, distopia e relações entre homem e máquina, com títulos de diretores como Jacques Tati, Michelangelo Antonioni, Rainer Werner Fassbinder, Edward Yang, Harun Farocki, Ridley Scott e Ana Vaz ( veja a programaçã completa ).

🗓️ Quando? Até 23 de agosto. 📍Onde? Caixa Cultural Rio de Janeiro - Unidade Passeio, Rua do Passeio, 38, Centro. 💲Quanto? Gratuito. 🧒 Classificação: Consulte a programação .

O Museu da História e da Cultura Afro-Brasileira (MUHCAB) recebe a exposição imersiva "Território Inventivo Pequena África", do Instituto CIRCOMUM. Com o conceito de recuperar a memória, a potência criativa e o protagonismo negro na formação da identidade nacional, a mostra oferece uma perspectiva histórica sobre a região que engloba sete bairros da área central e portuária do Rio de Janeiro.

A experiência une a ancestralidade à tecnologia, contando com maquetes hiper-realistas, painéis interativos sobre a diáspora, salas temáticas e recursos de realidade aumentada, onde o público poderá interagir e tirar fotos com projeções 3D de figuras históricas fundamentais, como Tia Ciata , Machado de Assis e Pixinguinha .

articles.title: Susan Sarandon leads tributes to Rocky Horror Picture Show co-star Tim Curry
articles.summary: Stars of stage and screen grieve the cult British actor, who has died aged 80.
articles.body:
Stars of stage and screen have paid tribute to cult British actor Tim Curry, who has died at the age of 80.

"What I loved about him most was his heart," said Oscar-winner Susan Sarandon, who co-starred with him in The Rocky Horror Picture Show.

Curry, who was born in the north-western English town of Warrington in 1946, passed away peacefully at his home in Los Angeles on Tuesday, said his manager. He had used a wheelchair since suffering a major stroke in 2012.

In a career spanning six decades, the prolific actor left his mark on both theatre and film, ranging from Home Alone 2 and Annie to Stephen King's It and The Hunt for Red October.

But he was perhaps best known for his zany role as the cross-dressing Dr Frank-N-Furter in The Rocky Horror Picture Show.

He first played the part on stage before the movie adaptation that propelled him to cult stardom.

Sarandon, who played the heroine Janet Weiss in the movie, praised Curry as "a funny, sexy, original".

"Thank you Tim for meaning so much to so many people."

Curry's longtime manager and friend Marcia Hurwitz confirmed he "passed away peacefully at his home in Toluca Lake, Los Angeles on August 25".

Australian actress Nell Campbell, who starred alongside Curry in The Rocky Horror Picture Show, told the BBC: "I feel like the head of our family has just died because he was the head of the Rocky Horror family."

Welsh actor Luke Evans, who played Frank-N-Furter in a Broadway revival, called Curry "a force, a bright fierce flame, an exquisite charm".

In a letter he recently wrote to Curry, Evans thanked him for his fearlessness and for "creating something so enduring, and for inspiring generations of actors to be a little braver than they thought they could be".

The official Rocky Horror Picture Show on Broadway account similarly thanked the late actor for "giving the world a little more freedom, a little more fearlessness, and through the tears in our eyes, the courage to BE IT" - a nod to Curry's delivery of the famous line from the musical: "Don't dream it, be it."

In a statement to Entertainment Weekly, writer and composer Richard O'Brien, who co-wrote the musical and film, remembered the actor as "a wonderful man by nature who was also a wonderful performer".

"He never sought attention and never put himself before the roles that he played," O'Brien said. "He was, in short, a good egg and class act."

Curry also starred in the 1996 film Muppet Treasure Island alongside Miss Piggy and Kermit the Frog.

He was one of the few humans "to have earned the title of honorary Muppet", the Muppets account posted on Tuesday.

"As a performer he was unparalleled – witty, charming, unnerving, and deeply funny. We will always consider it one of our greatest treasures to have been part of Long John Silver's crew," it added.

American comedy icon Carol Burnett shared a clip of Curry's turn as her smarmy brother in Annie, posting on social media that "nobody could play lovable villains better than he could".

Rob Schneider, who played the bellboy to Curry's uppity hotel clerk in Home Alone 2, also praised Curry as a "sensational character actor".

"A truly gifted performer of stage and screen, his one eyebrow could say more than most actors entire bodies," Schneider said.

"I am grateful to have the rare gift of watching him work, he made you better just standing near him."

Clue co-star and Better Call Saul actor Michael McKean said on social media that his last conversation with Curry was about "life and love and laughter".

"The grim physical state he found himself in has now ended, a blessing. Our blessing was that we had Tim Curry in our lives. RIP, my friend," he wrote.

Two other stars of Clue, where Curry played a butler, Christopher Lloyd and Lesley Ann Warren, also paid tribute on social media.

Lloyd shared a photo of Curry from the film along with a heart emoji and Warren called Curry a "dear companion in crime".

"The brilliant, hilarious, hysterically funny, magician of artistry has left us," she said.

"What an unbelievable joy to have shared a soundstage with him and to engage with such a master talent. I adored him. Bless his wild and inspired soul."

articles.title: Yayoi Kusama, whose art evoked hallucinatory wonder, dies at 97
articles.summary: Her hypnotic, unconventional works propelled her from near-obscurity to a place in the world's most prominent museums.
articles.body:
Yayoi Kusama, the beguiling Japanese artist who was a member of the 1960s avant-garde, disappeared from public view for decades and found global recognition late in life through her polka-dot paintings and mirrored, Instagram-friendly "infinity rooms," died Aug. 14 at a hospital in Tokyo. She was 97.

Her death was announced Wednesday in a statement on her website, which did not cite a cause.

Ms. Kusama, a largely self-taught artist, rose from near-obscurity to near-ubiquity in the art world, even as she battled mental health issues and lived for decades at a psychiatric institution in Japan.

Tenacious, obsessive and, in the eyes of her critics, relentlessly self-promoting, she became a pop-culture fixture, making brightly colored, instantly recognizable paintings, sculptures and installations that were exhibited at major museums and made her one of the world's top-selling contemporary artists.

Her work was immersive, hypnotic and repetitive by design. For her long-running "Infinity Nets" series, which began after she moved to Manhattan in 1958, she covered her canvases with delicately curved brushstrokes, dots or webbed lines. She later applied her approach to three-dimensional objects, including more than 20 of her "infinity mirror" rooms, reflective spaces that she filled with hundreds of kaleidoscopic LED lights or with silver orbs, polka-dot covered gourds and other eye-catching objects.

Ms. Kusama said she was inspired by hallucinatory visions she had experienced since childhood, in which she could hear the voices of flowers, pumpkins and dogs. Art served as a form of therapy: She wrestled with many of the vivid images in her head by re-creating them in her art, and at times was said to paint without interruption for 40 to 50 hours straight.

"I don't consider myself an artist," she wrote in a 1975 autobiographical essay, "Odyssey of My Struggling Soul." "I am pursuing art in order to correct the disability which began in my childhood."

By her own reckoning, she was an outsider many times over: a woman raised in wartime patriarchal Japan who broke into the male-dominated New York art scene, making her own mark alongside 1960s artists including Andy Warhol , Frank Stella , Claes Oldenburg and Donald Judd.

Like them, she was credited with helping move American art beyond abstract expressionism. Much of her work in that period featured a sexually charged blend of humor and provocation, including cheeky, handsewn phalluses — protuberances made of cotton-stuffed canvas and coated with enamel paint — that she applied to chairs, sofas, dresses and even rowboats.

Created as part of her "Accumulations" series, the works were a riposte to the patriarchy, she said, but also a way of "conquering" her fears around sex, which Ms. Kusama confronted more bluntly through naked "happenings" that she organized around the city, inspiring and mirroring performances by feminist artists such as Charlotte Moorman, Carolee Schneemann and Yoko Ono.

For a time, the happenings occurred weekly, taking on conservative taboos and also serving as protests against the Vietnam War. During her 1968 "Nixon Orgy" in Lower Manhattan, Ms. Kusama bluntly offered to have sex with the president-elect if he would call for a ceasefire. "Anatomic explosions are better than atomic explosions," she announced in leaflets distributed on the street.

The next year, she organized a "Grand Orgy to Awaken the Dead." Nude performers kissed and embraced in a fountain outside the Museum of Modern Art, in an unauthorized spectacle that Ms. Kusama described as a critique of the museum's focus on "dead" art, made by dead artists, over the work of the living.

Ms. Kusama's orgiastic happenings made front-page news, often accompanied by pictures in which she was shown wearing skintight, polka-dot unitards or posing nude.

To admirers, she was ahead of her time, blurring the line between her art and herself. Other tastemakers considered her an exhibitionist and seemed to share the assessment of New York Times art critic Roberta Smith, who wrote decades later that Ms. Kusama's happenings were "more like extended streaking incidents than actual performances."

Reflecting on her work, Ms. Kusama's manager, James Galotta, told The Washington Post in 1969: "We're not trying to change anybody's ideas. We just want them to think about alternatives. Yayoi is the kind of person who, if 500 years from now everybody was walking around nude, she'd be the only person wearing a dress."

Despite a fair amount of attention, Ms. Kusama withdrew from the art world in the early 1970s. Her mental health worsened over the years as she worried about other artists stealing her ideas. Her blatant hunger for media attention turned many art critics against her.

After a series of nervous breakdowns and suicide attempts, she checked herself into a Japanese psychiatric hospital in 1975. She became a permanent resident of the hospital in 1977, opening a studio nearby and making her art between the two spaces for decades.

With the rise of Instagram in the 2010s, viewers began waiting in line for hours to spend seconds (or, at best, a few minutes) inside one of Ms. Kusama's mind-bending infinity rooms.

First designed in the mid-1960s, the spaces — cosmic fun houses where the mirrored walls seemed to multiply each individual light into hundreds of shimmering stars — were exhibited at institutions around the world, including the Smithsonian's Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden, which brought together six of the rooms in 2017.

The exhibition was so popular, museum director Melissa Chiu said in a 2025 interview, that it broke the Smithsonian Institution's website twice.

"A whole group of visitors came to see the show who wouldn't ordinarily think of going to a museum," Chiu told The Post. "When we think of artists having moments, it's when they kind of transgress — or go beyond — just the art world, and we had all these visitors who didn't know her name, but they were coming to see her work." The venue held a smaller show in 2022.

Ms. Kusama capitalized on the attention, licensing her work for tote bags, shirts and key chains covered with her signature polka dot designs. She also branched into fashion, collaborating with Marc Jacobs on a 2012 Louis Vuitton collection, and became something of a fashion emblem in her own right, known for her distinctive red bob. Jacobs brought back some of her designs for a show in 2023.

By 2019, she was designing a balloon for the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade : a red tentacled figure with a bulbous nose, fishlike mouth and, of course, plenty of polka dots.

The youngest of four children, Yayoi Kusama was born in Matsumoto , near the center of Japan's main island, on March 22, 1929. Her parents ran a plant nursery and had a troubled marriage. She said her mother forced her to spy on her philandering father.

"He ended up having an affair with a geisha and deserted us to be with her in Tokyo," Ms. Kusama told the Guardian in 2009. "I was stuck in the middle of a long-running feud, and I felt mentally cornered."

By age 10, she said she was experiencing vivid hallucinations. She wrote in her 2002 autobiography that she encountered her first pumpkin — a human head-sized orb that spoke to her — at a seed farm she visited with her grandfather, and was drawn to its "generous unpretentiousness" and "spiritual balance." Violets, she said, also seemed to speak to her, and patterns overwhelmed her vision.

She began seeing a psychiatrist, who urged her to paint what she saw.

Her mother, who hoped Ms. Kusama would one day marry into a wealthy family and become a housewife, tried to stop her from becoming an artist, throwing away her paintings and insisting that she could only go to art school if she agreed to attend etiquette school as well.

Ms. Kusama worked in a factory during World War II, sewing parachutes for the Japanese army. After the war, she studied traditional Japanese-style painting at what became Kyoto City University of Arts. She began sending letters and her watercolor paintings to American artist Georgia O'Keeffe seeking advice, and O'Keeffe guided her to galleries that might show her work.

Ms. Kusama made her New York solo show debut in 1959, with a collection of abstract "Infinity Nets" paintings at the Brata Gallery that artist Judd, reviewing the show for ARTnews, praised her as "original" and "advanced in concept."

Starting out, Ms. Kusama was a relentless networker, hunting for patrons who could subsidize her rent and seeking out like-minded artists who could offer advice and community. (O'Keeffe, among others, helped her look for galleries to exhibit in.)

She moved around New York and eventually lived in what she described as a freezing, "much-too-large" loft with broken windows in Manhattan's Greenwich Village neighborhood. "I had only one blanket," she told ArtForum. "Since I could not sleep, I got up to face the canvas and continued painting meshes of a net till dawn. Day after day, I forgot my coldness and hunger by painting."

In 1962, she met Joseph Cornell , an artist 26 years her senior. He pursued Ms. Kusama with a deluge of letters, love songs and daily phone calls, and he gave her some of his work that she could sell to support herself. They settled into an intense platonic relationship. "I disliked sex, and he was impotent, so we suited each other very well," she recalled.

As Ms. Kusama began exhibiting at New York galleries, she accused some of her contemporaries of copying her work. She criticized Oldenburg's soft sculptures, made with fabric and stuffing, as imitations of her own phallus-covered chairs and objects.

When Warhol debuted cow-covered wallpaper at the Leo Castelli gallery in 1966, Ms. Kusama was devastated by what she considered the theft of her idea to plaster the walls as she had done a three years earlier for a solo show at the Gertrude Stein Gallery. She began covering the windows of her studio so other artists would not be able to peek inside.

Her frustration deepened in 1966, when artist Lucas Samaras garnered widespread attention for exhibiting a mirrored room at the Pace Gallery in New York. His show overshadowed Ms. Kusama's earlier forays into mirrored installations at the Castellane Gallery, where she had set up an infinity room filled with countless phalluses covered in red polka dots and, months before Samaras's show, exhibited "The Peep Show," an octagonal mirrored room that included openings allowing viewers to stick their heads inside to see thousands of dazzling lights.

Ms. Kusama said she fell into a deep depression and attempted suicide by jumping from her window. She survived unscathed, landing on a bicycle that broke her fall.

That same year, she showed up at the Venice Biennale uninvited, where she set up an unauthorized "Narcissus Garden." She marketed the 1,500 mirrored spheres as "your narcissism for sale," hawking them for $2 apiece. She recalled that when exhibition officials complained, she asked them, "Why can't I sell my art like ice cream or hot dogs?"

When she returned to New York, she continued organizing similarly controversial performances. By the end of the decade, the press had soured on her nude happenings and publicity stunts.

"Kusama, whose gross lust for publicity never leaves room for taste, managed to put on the year's most boring freak show," a Village Voice critic wrote.

Ms. Kusama's career fell into a lull when she returned to Japan in 1973, the year after the death of her partner, Cornell. After attempting suicide in 1975, she checked herself into the Seiwa psychiatric hospital in Tokyo, where she became a permanent resident and began writing semiautobiographical novels with titles such as "Manhattan Suicide Addict."

For nearly two decades, Ms. Kusama largely disappeared from the American art scene. She found her way back to the spotlight with help from Alexandra Munroe, an authority on modern and contemporary Asian art, who saw some of Ms. Kusama's sculptures at a gallery in Tokyo and spearheaded a 1989 retrospective at the Center for International Contemporary Arts, a new venue in Manhattan.

Reviewing the exhibition in the Times, Smith praised Ms. Kusama as "an artist who fits in everywhere yet stands alone," with a distinct sensibility that operated outside the confines of pop art, minimalism and surrealism. "Her work," she added, "is both pure and polymorphously perverse, intuitively systematic and a little mad."

The show launched a new era in Ms. Kusama's career. Invited to represent Japan at the 1993 Venice Biennale, she became the first artist from her country to be honored with a solo exhibition and covered the walls of the Japanese Pavilion with orange and black polka dots, filling a mirrored room in the center with matching pumpkins.

Ms. Kusama went on to have major exhibitions at museums including the Museum of Modern Art in New York, the Tate Modern in London and the Broad in Los Angeles. In 2006, she became the first woman to receive the Praemium Imperiale , a top Japanese art prize. She later opened her own museum in Tokyo.

In 2023, Ms. Kusama came under scrutiny when the art website Hyperallergic resurfaced a racist statement she had made in her 2002 autobiography, "Infinity Net," describing Black people as violent, primitive and hypersexual. She responded with an apology to the San Francisco Chronicle, just as her new show was opening at that city's Museum of Modern Art.

"My message has always been one of love, hope, compassion and respect for all people," she said. "My lifelong intention has been to lift up humanity through my art. I apologize for the pain I have caused."

Information on survivors was not immediately available.

Ms. Kusama spoke often about battling her mental illnesses to stay alive, attributing her survival to art. One of her late-career paintings, a black square flecked with orange and surrounded by a malevolent jagged-edged border, was titled, "I Who Have Taken an Anti-Depressant."

"I was given a sad life by fate, but I think I won a happy life," she told ArtForum in 1997. "Not one day has passed when I didn't think of suicide, but I'm very glad to be alive now."

articles.title: Actor Sunny Leone cleared in Rs 70L commission dispute case
articles.summary: MUMBAI: A sessions court has dismissed a criminal revision plea against actor Sunny Leone (Karenjit Kaur Vohra), her husband Daniel Weber and their ma.
articles.body: MUMBAI: A sessions court has dismissed a criminal revision plea against actor Sunny Leone (Karenjit Kaur Vohra), her husband Daniel Weber and their manager Sunny Rajani in a dispute over alleged unpaid commission of more than Rs 70 lakh for a Telugu film, holding that a commercial breach cannot be treated as a criminal offence unless fraudulent or dishonest intention exists from the outset.Complainant Omprakash Jain had approached the sessions court after a magistrate's court dismissed his private complaint in 2024. He had alleged cheating, criminal breach of trust and criminal intimidation, claiming Sunny Leone was given a role in the film through his efforts. Jain said there was an understanding that the accused would pay him a 10% incentive from the Rs 1.75 crore consideration connected with the engagement, but he received only part payment.According to the complaint, after Sunny Leone received Rs 35 lakh, Jain was paid Rs 1.75 lakh on Nov 26, 2000. He further claimed Rs 3.5 lakh was paid on July 20, 2022, but the balance amount of Rs 70 lakh and the corresponding 10% incentive were withheld.The record showed Jain had earlier sought an inquiry through the magistrate's court. On Dec 6, 2023, the magistrate refused to order a police investigation and directed him to proceed with verification under Section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In revision, Jain argued that the magistrate had failed to apply proper mind, wrongly treated the matter as civil, and rejected the complaint despite material allegedly showing cheating, fraud and breach of trust.Weber, Leone and Rajani, through advocate Rajkumar Mishra, opposed the plea, saying the complaint did not disclose the ingredients of offence.Additional Sessions Judge P A Sane noted that the documents included a tax invoice, two Form 16-A copies and a full-and-final settlement document in Jain's favour. The court said these reflected a commercial transaction. articles.title: A guide to August Bank Holiday weekend travel in the South East
articles.summary: Kent, Sussex and Surrey are expected to have some of the busiest roads in the country.
articles.body:
People travelling over the August Bank Holiday are being warned to expect busy roads and some rail line closures due to engineering works.

The south-east of England is expected to have some of the busiest roads in the country, as well as major transport hubs including Gatwick Airport and the Port of Dover, connecting the UK to mainland Europe.

We take a look at what travellers can expect over the long weekend:

The RAC says it estimates 20 million leisure trips will be made by car between Friday and Monday, as the summer holidays draw to a conclusion.

RAC breakdown spokesperson Harriet Hernando said: "Drivers should be ready for frantic Friday and think about setting off before 10am if they can.

"If the warm weather continues, people should be prepared in case they get caught in a traffic jam, by carrying plenty of water."

Transport analytics company Inrix identified a number of likely congestion hotspots, with the M25 anticlockwise from Junction 17 in Hertfordshire to Junction 12 in Surrey expected to be busy.

In Kent, Operation Brock - a contraflow system on the M20 coast-bound - has been removed from the early, as the Kent Resilience Forum says it is confident with regards to traffic flows for the remainder of the summer.

Operation Brock sees lorries heading to Dover queuing on one side of the M20 in an attempt to ease congestion.

Gatwick Airport says it has already experienced the peak of the summer - where 900 flights were scheduled to operate on the first, second and third Sundays of August.

Anyone intending to travel by plane over the long weekend is being encouraged by the airport to plan journeys in advance and book parking through the airport.

They have also been reminded to arrive when check-in opens - typically two hours before short-haul flights and three hours before long-haul flights.

The Port of Dover says that numbers of passengers this weekend are lower compared to previous weekends in the summer, but are still comparable to August bank holiday's year on year.

It says about 3,500 cars are expected daily on Friday, Saturday and Sunday.

A spokesperson for the port said: "Arrive at the port no more than two hours before a pre-booked sailing, and stick to the main routes (A20 and A2) to the port, to keep the town free-flowing for residents and businesses."

Southeastern will run a Saturday service on bank holiday Monday.

The line between Lewisham and Hayes is closed throughout the whole weekend, with buses replacing trains.

Thameslink and Southern services will run to an "amended" timetable on Monday.

On Saturday and Sunday, some late night trains between Brighton and Worthing/Littlehampton will be replaced by a bus.

Trains from Tattenham Corner/Caterham will terminate at Tulse Hill due to track renewal work between London Bridge and Tulse Hill.

The line between Lewes and Haywards Heath remains closed until Tuesday, as repairs to the railway continue following a derailment.

The South Western Railway line between Farnham and Alton will be closed all weekend, with buses replacing trains.

All lines through Effingham Junction are also closed all weekend, with trains diverted and buses in operation.

Great Western Railway services between Gatwick Airport and Reading might be busier than usual due to the Reading Festival taking place.

articles.title: Victorious Festival: What you need to know
articles.summary: Thousands of people are set to descend on Southsea this weekend as Victorious Festival returns.
articles.body:
Victorious Festival returns to Southsea Common this weekend.

Friday night will see Richard Ashcroft headline with The Black Keys on Saturday and Kasabian will close the festival on Sunday

The three-day festival on the seafront throws open its doors on Friday - Sunday from 11:00 - 23:00 BST with the site area closing on Thursday for final preparations.

Up to 80,000 ticketholders are expected to go to the festival each day. There's no entry or re-entry after 20:00.

Most of the seafront will stay open during the festival weekend along with attractions including South Parade Pier, The Pyramids, Exploria, Blue Reef Aquarium, Southsea Beach Cafe and Clarence Pier.

Southsea Castle, The D-Day Story and Southsea Splashpark are closed to the public for the festival from Thursday.

Arrangements can be made for visiting veterans wishing to access the D-Day Story.

They will reopen to the public from Monday 31 August.

In addition to this year's headliners the bill includes a vast array of music including Scissor Sisters, Faithless, Bastille, Nile Rogers and CHIC, The Streets, Pixie Lott, Basement Jaxx, Jessie J, The Vaccines, Kate Nash and Kelis.

As part of the city celebrating its centenary the Southsea Common Bandstand will offer panoramic views of the Solent and host performances the 100th band to perform at the Bandstand in 2026 will take to its stage during the festival.

Along with the music there is a roller disco and skate park show and a kids stage and professional wrestling.

Ideally walk, cycle or use public transport.

Buses are running from the Hard Interchange dropping off at Clarence Pier. All three train stations are within walking distance of the festival site.

If you are driving into Portsmouth there is no onsite car park for Victorious. Parking is at Lakeside Car park, which needs pre-booking and then you can get a shuttle bus to the festival.

Ferry services run from the Isle of Wight and Gosport and Hayling. The closest crossing to the festival site from the island is the hovercraft from Ryde - all need pre-booking.

Various road closures will be in place around the festival site when people leave between 22:30 and just before midnight each night.

To help people leave the festival safely at the end of each day, some roads close to Southsea Common will be temporarily shut to vehicles between 22:30 and just before midnight.

Clarence Esplanade will reopen from 08:00 on Bank Holiday Monday. Avenue De Caen will re-open later in the week.

Full travel details are available on the Victorious website .

If you're heading to the festival, it's worth checking the latest Southsea weather forecast on the BBC website.

The current outlook is breezy with light rain Friday and Saturday with thundery showers and a fresh breeze on Sunday and temperatures in the low 20s.

As always, make sure you're aware of any health risks and take steps to stay safe during the event - there are some top tips here .

It is card payments only across all bars and food stalls.

Some items, including chairs and large umbrellas, are not allowed at the festival along with flags with poles, drones and laser pens.

Drinks other than an empty water bottle and food (unless it is baby food - but no glass containers are allowed).

articles.title: El aire polar provocará mínimas por debajo de 10 ºC en agosto: zonas más afectadas
articles.standfirst: La caída de las temperaturas será generalizada en España
articles.summary: La caída de las temperaturas será generalizada en España
articles.body: Pese a que el mes de agosto comenzó con valores por encima de 45 ºC, la tendencia ha dado un giro por completo y, en plena recta final, estos valores apuntan a caer en las próximas horas y las mínimas en determinadas zonas de la Península podrían estar por debajo de los 10 grados. Todo ello como consecuencia de la entrada de aire polar que desplomará los termómetros. El aire frío ganará protagonismo entre este jueves, 27 de agosto, y el viernes. Durante ese lapso, las temperaturas sufrirán un intenso descenso en prácticamente toda España, siendo más acusado en la zona interior peninsular, donde se podrán registrar mínimas por debajo de los 10 grados. La mitad norte y oeste peninsular serán las áreas donde se vivirá esta caída de manera más notable. Durante la madrugada del jueves al viernes, según explica Meteored en un comunicado, se notará el descenso de forma más evidente y acaba extendiéndose a más zonas del país. Áreas de Castilla y León, interior de Galicia, Asturias, Cantabria y centro peninsular será donde esos valores mínimos sean tan inusuales. Aunque no de manera tan acusada, pero en ciudades como Lugo, Madrid, Cuenca o Vitoria las mínimas se moverán entre los 11 y 13 grados. Un contraste evidente respecto a lo que vivirá en el área mediterránea, donde ese aire polar no tendrá casi afectación, y es que Alicante, Mallorca, Barcelona o Valencia no bajarán de los 25 grados. De cara al fin de semana, en todo caso, los valores volverán a ascender en el país y el calor ganará protagonismo. Este jueves, 27 de jueves, la Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (AEMET) tiene activas varias alertas, siendo solo cuatro de ellas por calor en Andalucía, Aragón, Cataluña y Comunidad Valenciana. En Galicia, en cambio, hay alerta por lluvias y posibles tormentas, mientras que en Cantabria se esperan fuertes rachas de viento.

articles.summary: Yash-starrer ‘Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups’ has begun its theatrical run on a spectacular note. The Geetu Mohandas directorial crossed the Rs. 10.
articles.body: Yash-starrer ‘Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups’ has begun its theatrical run on a spectacular note. The Geetu Mohandas directorial crossed the Rs. 100 crore mark in India on its opening day, setting up strong expectations for its first weekend. As the film enters Day 2, the focus now shifts to whether it can sustain the momentum and add another substantial figure to its domestic total.Toxic: Movie ReviewThe immediate target will be to strengthen its Day 2 and weekend collections before eyeing the Rs. 150 crore India net milestone. The film’s next major challenge will be converting its enormous opening into sustained weekday business. A strong weekend could put ‘Toxic’ on course for the Rs. 200 crore domestic mark, while its worldwide haul could continue moving towards the next major milestone. The film also enters its run after surpassing the opening-day performance of ‘Dhurandhar’ in the early box-office race, adding another layer to the commercial narrative surrounding Yash’s return to cinemas. Sustaining that advantage beyond the opening day, however, will depend on audience word-of-mouth and the film’s hold over the coming days.'Toxic' Day 1 earnings'Toxic' collected a net of Rs. 101.10 crore across a massive 24,579 shows on Day 1, taking its total India gross to Rs. 120.75 crore. A closer look at the language-wise split shows the Hindi version leading the charge with Rs. 55 crore, followed by a strong showing from the Kannada version at Rs 23.30 crore. The Telugu version added Rs 16 crore to the tally, while Tamil and Malayalam contributed Rs 5.50 crore and Rs 1.30 crore respectively.Its overseas performance has been equally strong, with the film grossing Rs. 20 crore internationally on Day 1 alone. Combined with its domestic haul, this pushed the film's opening day worldwide gross to an impressive Rs. 140.75 crore, positioning it as one of the biggest single-day openers for an Indian film this year.'Toxic' Day 2 collection live trackingAs per Sacnilk, 'Toxic' is currently running across 12,159 shows and has collected Rs. 8.09 crore net so far in live tracking.This takes the film's total India gross collection to Rs 130.30 crore and its India net total to Rs 109.19 crore, with final Day 2 numbers still awaited.Language-wise, Hindi continues to lead the live count with Rs 4.76 crore, followed by Kannada at Rs 2.21 crore, Telugu at Rs 0.65 crore, Tamil at Rs 0.36 crore and Malayalam at Rs 0.11 crore.With evening and night shows yet to be reflected in the live figure, the language-wise totals are expected to move further before the final collection for Day 2 is reported.Day wise collections for 'Toxic'Day 1: Rs. 101.10 croreDay 2 [LIVE]: Rs. 8.09 croreTOTAL: Rs. 109.19 croreMore about 'Toxic'Directed by Geetu Mohandas, 'Toxic' casts Yash in a dual role as Raya and his son Ticket, tracing a sprawling gangster saga set against the backdrop of Portuguese-ruled Goa. The story follows Raya's rise to power alongside his sister Ganga, played by Nayanthara, his complicated relationships with Nadia, played by Kiara Advani and Mellisa, played by Rukmini Vasanth, and the eventual fallout with his son that drives the film's dramatic final act. The ensemble cast also includes Huma Qureshi, Akshay Oberoi and Tara Sutaria in key roles. The CBFC cleared the film with an 'A' certificate and no visual cuts, though it did direct the makers to mute and replace select words and add mandatory statutory warnings across its various language versions.DISCLAIMER: The box office numbers and data in this article are compiled from diverse public and industry sources.
